correctness.rationale: Each polygon is identified by its six integral exponent pairs as printed in both 2014 and 2015 figures. The six character evaluations are linearly independent on (F8*)². The torus map (x,y)→(x^-1,x^-3y) is an involution and coordinate scaling x³ is invertible. Direct algebra gives x³(A(x^-1)+b x^-3y+c x³y^-1)=A_rev(x)+b y+c x⁶y^-1, and since x⁷=1, x⁶=x^-1. Coefficient reversal is a bijection, hence these two six-dimensional code spaces are equal after an explicit monomial operator. A standalone GF8 implementation checks all 49 generator-row identities, both ranks six, and the coordinate permutation bijection. Different boundary lattice counts 4 and 3 independently establish non-lattice-equivalence. No experimental extrapolation is needed.

originality.rationale: The 2014 arXiv source and the 2015 published version explicitly state the exact equality of weight enumerators but leave this same named equivalence open as Conjecture 1.1. Its identity is now exhibited by an explicit 49-coordinate permutation and nowhere-vanishing diagonal weights. The 2020 dimension-seven sequel cites the earlier work and considers distinct 7-point questions; its inspected text gives no explicit transformation settling the six-point pair. Targeted literature and mathematical-record searches found no earlier statement or stronger classification providing this specific matrix. The historical priority of the direct transformation is not independently certified.
residual_risks: A later specialist article or unpublished note could have stated the same simple involution without indexing the original polygon names. The literature search is substantial but not a complete historical proof.

The proof is elementary and self-contained; publication priority requires independent human review despite the explicit original conjecture.

value.rationale: The original mathematical source explicitly identifies this precise F8 equivalence as its sole remaining dimension-six classification ambiguity and states the desired conclusion as Conjecture 1.1. A direct 49-coordinate transformation settles that natural outstanding classification question. The finite-field exponent wraparound explains a nontrivial phenomenon: non-lattice-equivalent polygons can yield monomially equivalent toric surface codes; the concrete involution is a reproducible witness rather than another enumerator coincidence.
